question: Name two optional pavement-marking features explicitly labeled in Figure 3D-1 at the roundabout.
model_answer: Direct Answer: Figure 3D-1 explicitly labels "Optional white diagonal markings" on the splitter-island approach area, and it also marks as "Optional" the yellow edge line placed around the inner (left-hand) edge of the circulatory roadway. (The YIELD word marking is likewise permissive per text, but the two clearly labeled optional features are the white diagonal markings and the yellow inner edge line.) Options (permitted): - "A yellow edge line may be placed around the inner (left-hand) edge of the circulatory roadway (see Figure 3D-1)…" - "Channelizing lines … and chevron and diagonal markings … may be used on the approaches to and within the circulatory roadway of multi-lane roundabouts to separate traffic lanes, discourage lane changing, and/or compensate for off-tracking of larger trucks and vehicles." - "YIELD (word) (see Figure 3D-1) and YIELD AHEAD (symbol or word) pavement markings may be used on approaches to roundabouts." Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Figure 3D-1 shows a callout reading "Optional white diagonal markings" pointing to the hatched white area near the eastern splitter island, and an "Optional" label with an arrow pointing to the yellow edge line around the inner edge of the circulatory roadway. - [Image 5] The full page view of Figure 3D-1 (p.596) confirms both labels: "Optional white diagonal markings" and "Optional" pointing to the yellow inner circulatory edge line (plus "Optional" callouts near the YIELD marking area). Citations: - Section 3D.03 Option §4 (p.605) - Section 3D.02 Option §5 (p.595) - Section 3D.05 Option §1 (p.605) - Section 3D.01 Support §4 (p.595) - Figure 3D-1 (p.596)
gold_answer: Optional diagonal markings in the splitter island and an optional wide dotted extension of the circulatory roadway edge line.
